comparisonToLocalRun.note: The two runs use different identities (fresh authority each time) and different installer builds (d302868b3 versus the exact merge). Both pass 17 of 17 with the same scenarios, the same N4-before-S5b order and the real-time soak. Differences are listed here, not hidden.

carryForwards.target: src/lib/multiplayer/server/InMemoryPlayerStore.ts and the P2J carry-forward that depends on this answer
carryForwards.status: OPEN DECISION for Root; this closure does not rule
carryForwards.item: Packaged evidence (both runs): after an authority restart the seats and public playerIds are unchanged (playerIds come from keys and the seat rows live in SQLite) and the production standalone server prints the InMemoryPlayerStore dev-only warning. Identities therefore survive a restart. Player profiles held by InMemoryPlayerStore (display name, avatar, lastSeenAt) are lost on restart. The record field matchRecovered=no is the spec any-socket-close heuristic: after the restart the authority log shows the GM and P1 sockets accepted and bound to campaign A and exactly one upgrade refused with reason=expired (the log does not name the player; the round-1 review attributed it to the P2 original seat-2 bearer, which had expired before the restart, and the second run has the same timeline: minted in S1/S2, expired during the soak, restart after expiry). The reading is inconclusive, not a product defect. Root rules one of: (a) no identity repair needed (identity is durable; profile loss is accepted and disclosed), or (b) register a profile-persistence follow-up unit. P2J depends on the answer. STEP2-RC-RERUN-1 should record recovery per profile.
optionsForRoot: (a) rule "no identity repair needed" and disclose the profile loss
(b) register a profile-persistence follow-up owner for InMemoryPlayerStore

carryForwards.target: PUT /api/campaigns/[id] and DELETE of a live-host campaign
carryForwards.item: From a guest profile viewing the HOST badge, the dashboard whole-record save is accepted by PUT /api/campaigns/[id] and an anonymous DELETE of a live-host campaign answers 204; the campaign socket takes the role from the verified bearer and is not affected. LSC-2P proves no implied server authority only through N4 (no host surfaces in the UI) and S1 (three distinct verified principals).
